findings.trigger: Open the debug logs (DebugLogsButton) and leave the message alone. At 270 s _auto_recreation_loop -> _recreate_view edits the message with a fresh LiveLogView (line 447) and cancels its own auto-refresh and recreation tasks, but never calls self.stop() and keeps self.message_ref. The OLD view still has its 300 s View timeout running, so 30 s later its on_timeout fires, disables its own buttons and edits the SAME message with `view=self` (the old, finished view) and the footer 'Live Logs view timed out' (lines 686-697). The fresh view installed 30 s earlier is thereby thrown out of the message; the user sees dead buttons after 5 minutes although the class comment promises 'auto-recreate before timeout'. If auto-refresh was running, the new view's loop keeps editing the message and re-installs its buttons on its next tick, so the damage is visible mainly in the static (not auto-refreshing) case, which is the default (DDC_LIVE_LOGS_AUTO_START False).
findings.suggestion: In _recreate_view, after the hand-over: clear self.message_ref (or set a `replaced` flag) and call self.stop(); in on_timeout, return early when the view was replaced (message_ref is None / flag set). Alternatively give the recreated view the job of stopping its predecessor.
findings.unsure_why: Depends on py-cord View semantics I cannot verify here: I assume the timeout task belongs to the view object and fires on_timeout even after the message has been edited with another view; nothing in the visible code stops the old view.

findings.trigger: info_extras() is documented 'Never raises', but only asyncio.TimeoutError is caught around the facts task. If get_container_facts(name) raises anything else (the container was removed between the status render and the press, Docker API error, NotFound), asyncio.wait_for re-raises it, info_extras raises, and StatusInfoButton.callback (line 960) catches only (RuntimeError, ValueError, KeyError). The interaction was already deferred (line 922), so the member sees the ephemeral 'thinking...' indicator and never gets an answer or an error message. player_list() by contrast wraps its work in a broad except for exactly this reason.
findings.suggestion: Catch Exception (with the same BLE001 justification as in player_list/image_update) around the facts await and set facts = None; or make StatusInfoButton.callback's error handler broad enough to send the error embed.
findings.unsure_why: I cannot see services/infrastructure/container_facts_service.get_container_facts; it may already swallow all errors and return None, in which case the promise holds.

findings.trigger: ContainerInfoAdminView (timeout 890 s) attaches four buttons; only ProtectedInfoEditButton.callback re-checks at the press (lines 222-229: current channel control permission OR _admin_may_control for THIS container). EditInfoButton.callback (271) and DebugLogsButton.callback (718) check nothing but the spam cooldown. (a) Channel loses its control permission while an admin view is open: for up to 15 minutes the edit-info modal still opens (and, if the modal has no check of its own, saves) and the container's logs are still shown, although the operator decided that old admin panels lose their effect immediately (SPEC Z5, 2026-09-16). (b) The comment at 216-222 says the view builder elsewhere 'does not know about container assignments' (review F3): if the view is built for a list admin in a status channel, an admin assigned to container A opens the display for container B and gets 📝 (edit B's info text) and 📋 (read B's logs) - exactly what the 🔒 button was fixed to refuse. Both siblings drifted from the one that was fixed.
findings.suggestion: Apply the same guard as ProtectedInfoEditButton.callback:222-229 at the top of EditInfoButton.callback and DebugLogsButton.callback (in DebugLogsButton after the defer, refusing via followup). TaskManagementButton lives in task_ui.py, outside this section, and should be checked for the same reason.
findings.unsure_why: Case (a) is certain from the visible code (a 15-minute window, rare). Case (b) depends on control_ui.py's view builder and on SimplifiedContainerInfoModal, which I cannot see; the modal may re-check on submit.

findings.trigger: A registered admin (admins.json, B2) presses the ℹ️ button on a status message in a status-only channel. has_control is computed from the channel permission alone (line 929) and the admin view is built only `if has_control` (948), so the admin gets the plain embed with no 📝/🔒/📋/task buttons. SPEC Z5 (clarified 2026-09-19) lists 'the info admin view' among the paths restored for admins in status channels, and ProtectedInfoEditButton.callback in this very file already allows `_admin_may_control` - a check that can never be reached through this door. The dropdown path (control_ui.py) and this button therefore decide the same question differently.
findings.suggestion: has_control = channel control permission OR _admin_may_control(interaction.user.id, self.container_name) (the same disjunction as line 225), so both doors agree; or, if the operator wants the button to stay channel-only, record that as a decision.
findings.unsure_why: Cannot see control_ui.py or tests/spec/test_z5_admins_act_in_status_channels.py; the operator may have restored the admin view only on the dropdown path deliberately.

findings.trigger: StatusInfoView is persistent (timeout=None) and reads the info config once when the status message is built (line 858); ProtectedInfoButton keeps that dict and hands it to PasswordValidationModal as container_info (1092). The operator then changes the protected password or content in the panel. A member presses 🔐 on a status message rendered before the change: the modal receives the old password/content. If the modal validates against container_info, the OLD password still opens the protected text and the NEW one is refused until the status message is rebuilt - the user believes the panel change is live. StatusInfoButton._generate_info_embed deliberately reloads fresh data (line 980-985 'to get latest protected info'); this button does not.
findings.suggestion: Reload the container info in ProtectedInfoButton.callback (get_container_info_service().get_container_info) and pass the fresh dict, or have the modal read it itself.
findings.unsure_why: PasswordValidationModal (enhanced_info_modal_simple.py) is outside this section; it may ignore container_info and re-read. Also unknown how often the status cycle rebuilds the view, which bounds the staleness.

findings.trigger: ContainerInfoAdminView carries a `message` reference, an on_timeout that deletes the message 'to prevent inactive buttons' and start_auto_delete_timer (885 s, before the 15-minute interaction token expires). On this path the view is built without a message (line 950), the followup.send result (955) is discarded, and the timer is never started. After 890 s the ephemeral info message keeps four buttons that answer 'This interaction failed'.

custom_ip 'play.example.org:2456' and custom_port '2456' set in the info form -> the line shows `play.example.org:2456:2456`. The ':' check at line 253 only prevents gluing the GAME port; a valid custom_port is always appended. The docstring says an address that already carries its own port is never glued.
findings.suggestion: Apply the ':' not in custom_ip guard to the custom_port as well (or strip the port from the address first).
findings.unsure_why: Depends on whether validate_custom_address (control_helpers.py, not visible) accepts host:port at all; if it rejects the colon, the line shows [Invalid Format] instead.

findings.trigger: The comment at 1008-1010 cuts custom_text to MAX_CUSTOM_TEXT because 'Discord refuses an over-long description', but the description also gets protected_content (uncut, line 1028), the player block (up to 20 names plus times) and the Docker facts. With a long custom text, a long protected text and a full game server the description exceeds 4096 characters; followup.send raises discord.HTTPException, which the handler at 960 (RuntimeError, ValueError, KeyError) does not catch. The interaction was deferred, so the member sees 'thinking...' and nothing else.
findings.suggestion: Truncate the joined description to 4096 (or cut protected_content like custom_text) and catch discord.HTTPException in the callback so the error embed is sent.
findings.unsure_why: MAX_CUSTOM_TEXT and the save-side limit on protected_content are outside this section; if both are small the sum may never reach 4096.

notes: Observations without a finding-grade trigger or clearly intended: (1) container_logs_text never returns an empty/falsy string (errors come back as text), so DebugLogsButton's `if log_lines:` else-branch (818) and manual_refresh's 'no logs retrieved' warning (595) are unreachable; a missing container is shown as log text inside a 'Logs' embed with live buttons - visible, not wrong. (2) container_logs_text: `except docker.errors.NotFound` would raise NameError if `import docker` itself failed; only relevant when the SDK is missing. (3) LiveLogView takes DDC_LIVE_LOGS_REFRESH_INTERVAL / MAX_REFRESHES from get_setting without a type argument; if the setting comes back as a string from the environment, asyncio.sleep raises TypeError, which _auto_refresh_loop does not catch - the footer would keep saying 'Auto-refreshing' while nothing refreshes. Cannot see get_setting's typing. (4) The Live Logs ephemeral message can only be edited for 15 minutes (interaction token); the 270 s recreation chain therefore silently ends after the third round with debug-level logs only. (5) StatusInfoButton.callback logs four INFO lines per press including the full list of channel permission keys ('Enhanced debug logging', 934-943) - noise, not a defect. (6) should_show_info_in_status_channel computes has_control and ignores it, returning True always; harmless, but the docstring promises a decision the code does not make. (7) info_extras' 2.5 s budget does not cover address_line's WAN-IP lookup, which runs afterwards with whatever timeout get_wan_ip_async has; on the dropdown path (outside this section) that answers without deferring, this could exceed Discord's 3 s. (8) player_list turns a cached 'unreachable' support verdict into 'The game server does not answer' without asking again (deliberate, comment 153-158); if the support service does not re-check, the display and JoinWatcher (which then never announces joins for that server) stay wrong after the game comes back. (9) _generate_info_embed: `fresh_info_config.get('custom_text', '').strip()` raises AttributeError on a hand-edited `custom_text: null`, uncaught by the handler at 960. (10) player_joins: a status hiccup (result.success False for one cycle) deletes the server from `known` (line 105), so the next cycle is a 'first look' and joins in that gap are not announced - conservative, matches the spirit of the docstring but not its letter (it only promises this for a failed player query). (11) player_joins._post: delete_after is a client-side timer; notices posted shortly before a bot restart stay for good. check() returns notices as 'sent' even when no channel could be resolved. (12) schedule_join_check reads cog.config; whether a panel change to 'player_joins' reaches it without a config reload cannot be seen here. (13) info_extras defaults allow_detailed_status to True when the key is missing; if the status cycle's CPU/RAM switch uses another default for the same key, the two would disagree - cannot verify.
